00_START_HERE.md

Sophia — unified continuation pack

Version 2.0 · 1 October 2026
Status: consolidated planning baseline and implementation instructions; not an implemented integration or a release.
Target: davidelaverga/Sophia · inspected main aadd192d66bb60dea6c2ba212cea5e192d704858.

One plan from the actual current state

This pack supersedes the September 24 v0.3 and cumulative v0.4 packs, the September 30 management/coordination continuation, and the October 1 v1.0 execution/Luis overlay as the forward planning and navigation authority. It folds their retained requirements into local specifications, goals, contracts and launch instructions. The earlier packs stay unchanged in the repository as historical references. Implementers do not have to reconcile those packs to determine the next work.

Supersession does not undo implemented behavior, close an unfinished acceptance case, rewrite frozen prompt assets, or authorize an operation. Current repository security rules, actual implementation contracts, current owner decisions and existing in-flight assignments remain binding. This pack explicitly records their differences from earlier planning text.

Start: current baseline → execution sequence → your assigned goal. Read only that goal's required architecture and bindings, not the whole archive into each agent session.

The product remains coherent

Sophia is the cooperative guide and creation workspace. The application owns purpose, accepted decisions, sources and sharing. dsh is the native reasoning/runtime base. Paperclip is the selected operational backend for explicitly admitted new work. Omnigent is the narrow owner-native coding bridge. Grok Bot is an optional owner-connected contributor, initially for private knowledge collection with two-way communication, not a substitute root runtime.

The first Grok result, its questions, source inventory and all intermediate material land in the personal account. Only an authenticated human's Share with the team publishes a selected immutable version. Sharing is not mission acceptance. Full personal-assistant design.

Read by responsibility

Reader Starting material Next action
Davide / product and backend product/releases, baseline, decisions Continue M03; bind SCM without reopening the runtime selection; assign the optional personal-assistant lane explicitly.
Luis / implementation and integration Luis track, UI contract Preserve merged room; integrate current PR source; build creative and private-package views against real contracts.
Implementation agents implementation launch or Luis launch One scoped goal-session, exact branch/source and file ownership.
Codex / operator and independent reviewer operator launch, operation protocol Read-only discovery first; only separately authorized effect batches.
Bot owner / configured assistant connection guide, single template Review native account/auth/routine steps; qualification is not automatic provisioning.

What is immediately actionable

Continue PR32 on its own history and issue #31. At inspection its latest head is bb25f058…; S5b part 1 is in source, while remaining PDF UI, voice/text and hosted qualification stay open. Preserve PR35 → PR30 personal-space work on its existing stack, not an invented substitute project. SCM-00 is a short documentation/binding refresh, not a repeated PR29 deployment campaign. Luis can prepare image/prototype and coordination UI in parallel with their actual backend owners.

The Grok lane is included in the continuation but is not an added prerequisite for the core R1 team release. Its first live gate needs owner-private storage, scoped authentication, durable messages and exact sharing; it does not need a complete production personal Companion, all native engineers, or a cross-owner Bot swarm.

Contents and evidence

All goals and aliases · architecture map · code/integration map · Paperclip specification · source register · coverage · validation · install proposal.

READER.html is a self-contained offline reader. All required plan documents are in this directory with portable relative links. External pinned source links require access to their repository/service; they are evidence, not missing plan chapters. JSON schemas and executable design rehearsals are proposed contract/design checks, never database or provider acceptance.

01_PRODUCT_AND_RELEASES.md

Product scope and cumulative releases

Purpose

A small creative team should turn a partly formed idea into useful work, review what was actually produced, and carry decisions and learning into the next attempt. Ordinary conversation remains valid. Not every utterance creates a task, issue, model review, or permanent memory.

Sophia presents one coherent experience across Converse, Explore and Build. It may coordinate multiple execution resources, but the user should not have to operate competing agent managers. Personal space and the team workspace are different audiences; a resource connection never silently joins their context.

R1 — Create and coordinate together

R1a: current room plus useful research

Keep main's actual room, Chat/Brief side panel, text-mode behavior, mission ledger, consent and native bridge. Finish the active SMC-M03 work: sourced Markdown/PDF from the selected dsh research route, versioned Knowledge/report readers, usable output/download, and actual authorized voice/text and hosted acceptance. A Markdown success with no PDF is partial for a PDF request. Do not rebuild already-authored registry, byte store, parser or UI under a second feature name.

R1b: genuine creative work

Deliver intentional Google/OpenAI image generation and comparison, selected bytes retained for edits and handoff, a supported React/TypeScript/Vite prototype, Luis's Preview/Source/Diff editor, a no-secret isolated build/preview and source-preserving handoff to engineers. Selected prior knowledge can enter through explicit import with coverage and current-decision reconciliation. Report, HTML, deck and image-based PPTX output obligations remain; M03 does not close all format work.

R1c: three engineers and one reviewed application

Davide contributes Codex and Claude Code; Luis contributes Claude Code. Each is separately owner-authorized. Use the Paperclip operational path, real peer dialogue, evidence-based progress review, owner-specific waits and honest capacity observations. Show a meaningful pre-steer risk choice, source-preserving handover when needed, and a real app candidate reviewed in Sophia with both change and preservation constraints checked. Use all three resources when their contributions are useful, not artificial parallelism.

A smaller SCM source-review outcome may ship earlier. It does not silently reduce this full product acceptance. R1 is complete only when the original S1-14 episode and retained format/creative promises are demonstrated or specifically re-scoped by Davide.

Optional R1 contribution slice: owner-connected personal assistant

The first Bot use is gather scattered personal knowledge into a private package, with Sophia ↔ Bot questions, answers, corrections and blockers from the first accepted integration. Review happens in the owner's personal account; a specific shared version then enters the team. The feature can ship beside the team release when its own gates pass. Lack of a personal subscription or inability to connect a Bot must not block ordinary Sophia use.

One template contains the cooperation, knowledge packaging, research/report and review methods. A knowledgeable existing assistant can use the same skill. No catalog of mandatory specialist Bots. Template import does not prove inherited memory, tool availability, security isolation or a completed connection.

R2 — Precise cooperation and mobile control

Enforce exact source-backed revisions and protected-sibling checks for supported artifacts. Add Storybook/MSW scenarios and Playwright checks, with simulation, replay and actual application evidence kept distinct. Introduce supported in-app native answers, opt-in PWA notifications and mobile controls over the same current action identities. Extend consented discussion-following, selected vision, EN/IT/ES behavior and actual hands-free navigation. Retain selected Notion, Supabase and Vercel workflows without making their connectors a launch prerequisite.

For Bots, qualify one browser/application review and one environment-specific long-running task where the owner's configured environment provides real additional value. Cloud execution continuing after the user disconnects is not itself unique to Bots; Sophia-hosted workers should also do that. Local files and private-network routing still depend on the relevant device being available. Full local GUI control through Cua is a separate optional qualification, not the initial collection requirement.

R3 — Continuing, adaptive project work

A bounded standing mandate governs multi-week work. Real reset/availability observations can reconsider queued work without expanding permission or spending. Deliver a useful Sophia-native full-stack implementer, an evaluated small execution portfolio and a reviewed procedural-improvement loop with exact versions and rollback. Use the product repeatedly with an external team, including nontechnical contribution, and export source, decisions and remaining work in a portable form.

Cross-owner assistant cooperation is later gated work: dynamic roles, allowed peer edges and direct software delivery, no central model relaying every message. Prefer complementary access/expertise over duplicate generic research. Preserve native engineering and personal assistant resource classes rather than advertising equal controls.

Not prerequisites or promises

Workspace Agents remain deferred beyond the first release; organizational customer need and verified lifecycle/spend controls must justify reopening. Personal dots, Instinct and Muse are not selected runtimes. The ChatGPT-native/plugin edition is a distinct explored direction, not an implicit dependency here. Jev/Decisions API, Mobbin retrieval and broader computational environments remain optional measured opportunities. No paid fallback, automatic account purchase, general scraping, unlimited autonomy, or inferred private-to-team memory sharing is introduced.

See deferred decisions and all-goal coverage.

PR32: reuse what has advanced

The active branch includes report/source readers, a SigV4 Storage-only byte-store adapter, provenance, the single config/specialists.json registry, immutable attempt routes, cache/compaction accounting and reservation/settlement, Tavily/Jina access with disclosure and URL guards, durable Markdown report publication, Knowledge/report UI and source revocation behavior.

S5a includes the confined PDF kernel, render jobs, the renderer API and supervisor. S5b part 1 adds @sophia/report (the shared Markdown parser and service-owned PDF template), migration 0031, research_render_pdf, output inspection and exact-draft rendition publication. The service prints the source; the model does not directly author the printable HTML for this research path.

The remaining named slice is S5b part 2: PdfView, PDF rows and partial-delivery state, render_research retry and CSP. S6 adds the versioned guide 1.2 voice/text handlers and correct notices. S7 is compatibility and real hosted acceptance. OP-C renderer host qualification and the existing Codex reviews stay on issue #31.

The branch records local PostgreSQL, real Chromium and runtime crossing checks. It explicitly does not claim live Sol/Tavily/Jina calls or hosted effects. Do not combine those reports into a fresh test verdict. Its state file still has an older candidate_commit/migration summary while its test list and next action include S5b/0031; use the fresh branch head plus exact section evidence, and repair state bookkeeping in that mission.

Personal-space integration and new Bot dependency

PR35 supplies owner-private data/API. PR30 supplies the Home/Personal/Work layout, privacy curtain, same-owner reauthentication and proposed call retention across places. Main's Home currently ends the room; PR30 changes that while preventing hidden projects from taking keys or attention. A combined candidate must explicitly test the selected behavior.

The personal Companion is rehearsal-only and refused in production. The new private Bot job inbox is an asynchronous work object, not an unanswered conversational turn. It can rely on qualified personal storage/review without requiring a complete personal generative Companion. Optional personal Sophia assistance needs its own owner-scoped runtime and allowance; never create a fake team project to bypass that boundary.

The existing D5 remains no ambient private retrieval into the project. The new package-sharing operation is a second explicitly specified publication type, not permission for the team to read private history. Exact carried notes retain their own existing contract.

Reservations and shared files

Current main's source migrations are 0001–0020. PR35 owns A10/0021; PR32 owns A11/0022–0031 at this read. These are source reservations, not an inspected hosted migration ledger. Discover further reservations before allocating any new ID; this pack ships no deploy-ready new migration number.

Luis integrates App.tsx, route.ts, useProjectRoute.ts, SidePanel, shared call switches and keyboard/focus behavior. The M03 author owns its evolving artifacts/registry/renderer contracts until a real handoff. One writer owns generated contracts and locks in each integration window. Use the actual reviewed branch, not copies selected from unrelated commits.

Evidence that must not be overstated

PR29's report does not prove two-person speech quality, a fresh OAuth/passkey ceremony, or a live dsh model turn. PR32's checks do not prove provider authorization or hosted PDF availability. A template/configured plugin does not prove a functioning Bot connection. This pack's executable tests cover documentation and design models only.

03_DECISIONS_AND_SUPERSESSION.md

Decisions, supersession and conflict resolution

Effective planning hierarchy

  1. Current owner decisions and repository security/effect rules remain controlling.
  2. Actual source and dated evidence determine what exists; they do not authorize new scope.
  3. This v2.0 pack is the cumulative forward plan, including the explicitly retained contracts and current in-flight continuation.
  4. Later approved feature changes identify the exact clause, contract and goal they amend.
  5. Previous packs and older alternative architectures are history/evidence only.

Do not use "newest file wins" to replace source permissions or to treat a PR author's statement as a fresh direct owner approval. Installation changes navigation, not runtime. An in-flight mission keeps its author, issue, allowance, active attempt and current controller.

Unresolved decisions with bounded consequences

PS-RUNTIME: select and qualify an owner-only private Companion only when that feature is commissioned. It is not silently funded through a Bot subscription or inherited team runtime.

PA-AUTH: prove the actual Grok OAuth flow and credential subject. Assume an owner connection, not per-Bot attestation, unless evidence establishes more.

PA-WAKE: verify the current webhook's result/continuation behavior. Missing API idempotency/stop/status is a capability limit; no undocumented endpoint substitution.

PA-RELEASE: the optional assistant track is in this continuation, not a compulsory core-R1 dependency. A reviewed release disposition names whether its own gates are met.

SCM-IDENTITY: use the management pack's company-scoped Sophia integration principal, distinct from the human initiator carried in an authenticated envelope. Do not revert to earlier unqualified user-ID impersonation or an admin credential plus a claimed actor.

SOURCE/PROVIDER RIGHTS: owner access is not automatic permission to export employer/client data. Qualification records permitted uses and actual data handling. No legal clearance or commercial reseller status is inferred.

The exact legacy-to-current mapping is in coverage. Planned statuses are not application records and do not authorize releases.

VALIDATION.md

Validation and evidence boundaries

This pack is a planning deliverable. Documentation and in-memory design checks are not product acceptance.

Reproduce the checks

Use Python 3.11 or later. Install the documentation-only dependencies from scripts/requirements.txt in a separate environment; do not merge them into Sophia's runtime dependencies.

python -m pip install -r scripts/requirements.txt
python -B scripts/validate.py
python -B scripts/build_reader.py
python -B scripts/check_reader.py

The last command needs a system Chromium binary (default /usr/bin/chromium, overridable by CHROMIUM_PATH). These scripts do not call an AI provider or mutate the application, repository, database, account settings or deployment. The browser checker loads the generated HTML bytes and blocks external requests.

Structural coverage

The executable validator checks portable links and Markdown headings, JSON parsing, every original goal's mapping, SCM and frontend coverage, unique work/acceptance IDs, valid dependencies without cycles, canonical launch prompts, and positive/negative proposed-schema examples. It rejects font-file payloads. External source URLs retain their access and historical qualifications; this is not a fresh network availability check for every source.

Machine-readable validation report · Coverage map · Source/reading limits.

Design rehearsal

The local model tests intended owner isolation, exact-version publication, message/wake/claim separation, duplicate requests, and erasure/late writes. The model has no network, production OAuth, real database transactions, concurrency, file store, browser agent or provider billing. Passing it establishes consistency of this executable specification only.

Design test output · Test scope · Model source.

Reader checks

The standalone HTML reader is tested at desktop and phone widths for contents, full-text search, internal navigation, missing anchors, page errors and horizontal page overflow. Those checks concern this documentation interface, not Sophia Studio or iOS Safari.

Reader browser report · Reader link map.

Recorded results

The final validation passed for all 24 original-goal mappings, nine SCM missions, 17 frontend packages, and the 44-record goal/alias map. The 23 proposed-schema examples include 12 deliberately invalid cases; all behaved as specified. The 26 in-memory design tests passed. The offline reader passed navigation/search and all-document width checks at 1440 × 1000 and 390 × 844, with no page errors or external requests. Exact current link/file counts are in the machine-readable reports.

What remains unexecuted

All 323 product acceptance specifications in the catalog remain not_run by this delivery. Prior repository and hosted reports remain separately attributed; their achievements are not reset. No new Paperclip, Omnigent, Grok, local computer, subscription usage, live personal Companion, model route or hosted release is marked accepted here.

The ZIP's SHA256SUMS.txt covers packaged files other than itself. Validate it after extraction using sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS.txt where available. Rebuilding generated reports/readers legitimately changes their manifest hashes; regenerate the manifest only for a new reviewed pack version.

architecture/01_SYSTEM_AND_AUTHORITY.md

System and authority

Sophia separates human meaning, operational work, native execution, media, and presentation. The application owns the accepted mission, people and source grants, immutable candidates, decisions and publication. Paperclip owns issue/assignment/dependency/wake/review/recovery only for explicitly admitted work. dsh owns its model/tool/inbox lifecycle. Omnigent mediates owner-local native sessions. Grok is a hosted contributor with a narrower externally verified capability set.

Two levels of work, not duplicate task boards

A Sophia work contract names the outcome, accepted mission/source/criteria revisions, resource authority and acceptance owner. Paperclip issues are operational pieces serving it. Map stable identities and generations; display upstream operational status as a projection, not another editable Sophia status. A provider session is execution evidence, not the team's definition of completion.

Micro-operations can remain within an admitted attempt. Neither every utterance nor every peer message requires its own operational issue. A private knowledge-collection job remains in the owner-only application domain. Do not put even its title or source list in a shared Paperclip company. Later published work may have a new team operational binding; no simultaneous private/project scheduler for one attempt.

Effect authority is checked at the boundary

Derive actor from authenticated API context. Verify membership, contribution grant, current source eligibility, expected revisions, controller epoch and payer before sending an effect. A room holder, a model label, an imported document, an agent message or a displayed account name grants none of these rights.

The Paperclip integration principal is an actual restricted company member. The initiating Sophia actor is separately authenticated in a signed bounded envelope; never silently substitute an admin token with a userId parameter. Provider/native logins remain owner-held. An assignment authorizes only its specified role, not access to every resource its owner possesses.

State and recovery

Record intent and an outbox entry transactionally before external delivery. Durable acknowledgement, external acceptance, native incorporation, candidate arrival, review, acceptance and deployment are different observations. Missing evidence stays unknown. No distributed exactly-once guarantee is asserted across independent databases, native logs and provider effects.

Retire old grants/epochs before cancellation. Reconcile uncertain effects before retry, reassignment or source takeover. A database writer flag is not OS isolation. Existing attempts retain their current controller; migration requires stop/drain, source snapshot and a single new continuation owner.

Outages

Paperclip outage may block new managed work but cannot disable the existing conversation/living brief or direct native safety controls. Provider quota exhaustion cannot make Stop unavailable. Optional observability cannot become admission, recovery or acceptance truth. Private import unavailable is an optional capability failure, not a reason to route personal data through the team.

Detailed coordination lifecycle · private boundary.

architecture/03_STUDIO_AND_MEDIA.md

Studio, media and cross-feature interaction

Preserve the implemented room

Converse uses the actual main composition: the room center holds Sophia, participants and dock; Chat and Brief are mounted tabs in a right-hand panel. Unsent text, manual brief edits and per-viewer focus survive switching. Explore and Build put the actual asset/source at the center; no older centered-chat restoration.

Server project state, viewer state and media state are independent. A new snapshot cannot erase a draft. A component unmount cannot cancel work. A participant's view change cannot move another participant or grant source-edit authority.

View opens an object locally. Discuss references it. Focus together changes shared focus only for people following. Change work admits an authorized operation against a real target. The host confirms each material effect before narration says it happened.

One candidate through several views

Preview, Source, Diff, Sources and History refer to the selected exact source/version. New output is offered, not silently substituted while somebody reviews an older version. The last useful candidate remains visible during authorship, failure or conflict. Downloads verify the selected bytes/hash, not a changing latest URL.

Use the current report viewer and shared pure presentation helpers. A data-only Markdown view never becomes an arbitrary HTML execution context. Application preview requires an isolated origin and an explicit frame/selection contract; unembeddable third-party pages get an honest external route, not stripped security headers.

Real media state

Continue raw LiveKit ↔ Gemini media bridging, admitted input-floor/exchange, observed playback generations, selected visual frames and correct speaker/inputMode attribution. Barge-in clears old audio, not unrelated background work. Stop Looking, Stop Speaking, End exchange, leave room, Hold/Stop work and disconnect resource are separate controls. Result completion does not reopen an ended voice exchange.

S2 discussion-following is opt-in, track-attributed and governed by current consent. No biometric inference, hidden microphone activation, default ambient transcript retention or retired Tone Scale. One participation decision is used only for the following lane; ordinary invoked voice remains direct Gemini. Test EN/IT/ES, quoted names, negation, overlap, numbers and correction.

Keyboard, accessibility and mobile

Follow the real CONTRIBUTING contract. Typing a letter must not activate microphone/camera/screen sharing. Modal and hidden views do not compete for keys. Focus returns to a meaningful control after sheets close. Active sending, errors, mute/stop/leave remain reachable on phone overlays. Routine progress should not create a screen-reader announcement per event. Test zoom, coarse pointer, reduced motion, color-independent state and actual narrow layouts.

PR30's proposed cross-place call retention differs from main. Integrate it intentionally: hidden project keeps no key/attention ownership; switching to a different project ends the former call. Its privacy curtain is device UI, not universal revocation or permission to read private material in the room.

Personal assistant surfaces

A personal import job and message thread use personal queries/caches/notice channels. Locking personal view clears/hides sensitive client material without claiming remote computation stopped. architecture/04_ARTIFACTS_AND_CREATION.md

Sources, creative work, output and review

A single product artifact lifecycle

Reuse canonical source/byte/version primitives from M03. Each image, report, prototype, screenshot or deck has source identity, bytes, provenance, availability and current acceptance. Rendering and exporting create versions/renditions; they are not accepted mission changes. Personal and team permissions stay distinct even when common storage code is reused.

Images

Retain two intentional provider adapters: Google image generation/edit and OpenAI direct Images. Selected model snapshots/request recipes are dated qualification inputs in the binding, not assumptions about current availability. Do not fan out to every provider automatically. A clear authorized comparison requests both, stores actual bytes and records the configuration/outcome. Refusal, no image or uncertain acceptance remains visible. Selection performs no generation and preserves alternatives. Editing uses an exact selected asset/version and emits a new candidate.

Runnable source

The first supported prototype remains React/TypeScript/Vite. Preserve selected assets, tokens, interactions, dependency lock and mock-to-real boundaries. Luis's lazy bounded CodeMirror Source view is not a new IDE or browser shell. Opening source is read-only; editing requests explicit writer takeover and waits for real settlement where necessary. Submit patches against expected hashes and retain drafts on conflict.

Build scripts run with no API, native-login or cross-project secrets in a separate constrained workspace. Source/preview/export identity must agree. Failed builds retain the last useful preview. A target repository with a different stack gets a truthful adaptation plan, not a zero-rework promise or screenshot recreation.

Report, HTML, PDF and deck outputs

M03 owns Markdown/PDF research and its deterministic service template. Other HTML/deck work remains S1-13. Retain the three JS donor kernels' useful rendering/compilation parts, not their Python/runtime wrappers or insecure sandbox flags. Preserve ordered slide source, notes, language, images and preview PNGs. Image-based PPTX is exported from editable HTML; it is not natively editable PowerPoint shapes/text unless another qualified path is added.

Use explicit immutable source packages, source-root checks, asset closure, measured layout checks and actual output bytes. Do not report unknown overflow as zero. No renderer host may inherit provider credentials, broad mounts or a public network just to make rendering pass. The M03 kernel already authored is the PDF continuation; deck extraction remains distinct.

Review and precision

S1 coreview binds a real preview to source/environment/mocks. The user interacts or selects a target, clarifies material ambiguity, and supplies change plus preservation intent. The lead sends that to the current worker and checks the returned candidate. A source/DOM visual selector is not write authority.

S2-02 strengthens this into source-enforced editing: allowed target sources only, complete diff and protected-sibling hashes, meaningful rendered/behavior checks, expected-base CAS and rollback. Cross-cutting CSS/API changes need expanded scope. Imported flattened PDFs/PPTX do not acquire lossless editability. Never silently use whole-document regeneration because a target is ambiguous.

Browser review by a personal assistant

A Bot review may inspect a specified candidate, route, limited test account and journey and return observations/screenshots. It does not replace executable test coverage or grant source/deploy write access. Returned screenshots are governed artifacts; scan for personal account data before sharing. Cloud browser, local files and Cua desktop control are distinct qualification modes.

architecture/05_CONTEXT_PRIVACY_AND_LEARNING.md

Context, personal/team boundaries and learning

Current truth versus recalled material

Mission decisions and accepted constraints are current application records. Notes, imported research and source documents provide evidence. Derived summaries or wiki pages are rebuildable projections. A provider memory, chat log or old AI answer cannot override a newer accepted decision.

Use direct current-state reads first, then bounded scoped search/read when needed. Context packets identify source/version, eligibility and relevant decisions. Don't load entire histories into every role. Unsupported or unreadable imports carry explicit coverage; no fabricated reconstruction of missing attachments.

Source narrowing applies to every copy we control

Correction and withdrawal affect future queries, caches, source packets, resumed workers and derived displays. Track source dependence so revocation cannot be bypassed by a previously summarized packet. Rebuild an eligible context rather than reopening a raw old log that contains revoked material. Report remaining external copies honestly; app deletion cannot prove provider-wide erasure.

Owner-private data first

Personal conversations/notes and assistant jobs/packages are owner-only, including metadata, source lists, messages, notification bodies, caches and search embeddings. Project administrators are not personal-account owners. No private job details go into a shared Paperclip company or shared Sophia prompt. D5 remains no ambient personal retrieval.

An assistant import does not automatically become a permanent personal memory. It is a reviewable package. Sharing is human publication of selected exact bytes and redacted metadata into one permitted workspace. Project acceptance is separate. Keep carried-note and package-share types distinct, with explicit correction/withdrawal semantics.

Learning closes a useful cycle

After a result, distinguish observation, interpretation and proposed next action. Retain evidence, uncertainty and no-change outcomes. An accepted useful lesson enters the next relevant brief; this basic behavior does not wait for a global self-improvement system.

Procedural optimization later proposes a small versioned skill/recipe change from comparable evidence. Preserve exact baseline, candidate diff, regression/holdout cases, safety/cost effects, promotion approval and rollback. The model cannot declare improvement solely because it wrote a better-sounding prompt. Existing active attempts keep their recipe identity.

No automatic change of identity, safety, personal memories or voice doctrine. No reward for engagement, emotional uplift, disclosure or forced positivity. No raw personal package contributes to shared optimizer/tracing data without a separate governed purpose and consent.

Resource-aware cognition

M03's immutable execution-route and accounting layer is the initial control foundation. SCM capacity planning reasons over observed owner windows, contribution reserves and outstanding commitments, not a fungible wallet. Optional classifiers can choose among permitted workflow actions; they never determine authentication, exact arithmetic, approvals or membership. Decisions API/Jev use is a separate qualified route, not a mandatory paid dependency.

architecture/06_OPERATIONS_AND_RELEASES.md

Operations, testing and releases

Source control and current contracts

Use actual AGENTS/CONTRIBUTING rules, exact Node24.21.0/pnpm11.7.0 and frozen dependencies. Preserve runtime artifact identities and gate behavior. Updating a bundle/lock requires the repository's identity-recording process and affected tests; a plan file never changes a running route. Fresh SQL/amendment IDs are allocated from active branches and the actual target ledger, not guessed from an old example.

Reader-first release

Current API/bridge/Studio readers must understand new records before any writer emits them. Keep old record readability through rollback; do not delete new data to make an older runtime start. Qualify renderer/storage access and credentials separately, with least privilege. No sandbox-disabled fallback or secret-bearing browser proxy.

An operation request binds exact candidate/tree/artifacts, environment, affected contracts/migrations, preconditions, effects, allowance, expiry, verification and recovery. The operator verifies the actual deployed tuple and previous receipts, then executes only approved steps. An owner approval is separate from a coding agent's request. No provider, subscription, schedule, account creation or hosted mutation is authorized by this pack.

Evidence layers

A labelled UI fixture proves a view. A schema fixture proves structural validation. A pure design model proves only that model. PostgreSQL/RLS tests prove their actual executed database cases. Native/provider tests prove the exact route exercised. A source merge does not prove a hosted release. A completed run does not prove delivered bytes or product acceptance.

Use existing production reports as attributed historical evidence. Do not reset all goals to not_started, and do not mark old reports as rerun. An unavailable required environment is blocked evidence, not a skipped criterion called passed.

Focused adverse tests

Prioritize uncertain delivery, stale source/CAS, owner mismatch, revoked eligibility, source/credential leakage, delayed cancellation, tool-budget accounting, disconnected observers, private notifications, and simultaneous migration/route changes. Test timers with fake time where possible rather than waiting days or burning a user's quota to manufacture an outage.

The private assistant gate additionally tests that team search, source readers, caches, feed and prompts reveal neither private content nor metadata; immutable shared versions survive private edits appropriately; erasure blocks late retries; and webhook transport uncertainty does not silently incur another provider run.

Rollback and control

Rollback of a live route first blocks new admission and resolves active effects. A feature flag does not transfer controller ownership or revoke an owner's OS credentials. Keep the old source and exact effective writer settled or isolated before reassignment. Prompt/version rollback applies to new attempts; history remains attributable.

Pause future Bot activation by the available native routine controls and revoke Sophia access as needed. Neither operation proves that already-running cloud computation ended. UI/receipts must preserve that distinction.

Stop conditions

A session ends with a useful tested slice or a precise blocker and next owner. Do not run endless architecture loops, poll through a model, or weaken acceptance because a problem is inconvenient. The full founder episode remains distinct from smaller release slices. See working protocol.

Goal sessions

SCM-08-G1 — Evidence slice

Build: Select one repeatable coordination defect, matched task/route episodes and measurable outcome. Separate missing capability from a procedural mistake. Record confounders and gaps.

Build: Propose one allowed recipe/skill change with exact base hashes, scope, expected effect and rollback. A Reflection Coach-like proposer is optional, not presumed implemented upstream.

Handback: Proposal changes no identity/voice/safety/consent/personal memory or unrelated global settings.

SCM-08-G3 — Executed validation

Build: Run reproducible regression and held-out cases within a separate approved allowance. Compare accepted outcomes, corrections, cost and latency; hypothetical replay is not execution.

Handback: Evidence supports promotion or rejection; no victory claim based only on an LLM’s suggested diff.

SCM-08-G4 — Human promotion and rollback

Build: Apply exact reviewed bytes under compare-and-set, record the new recipe version, use only on new eligible attempts and rehearse rollback.

Handback: A stale base refuses; current active attempts remain bound to their earlier identity; rollback restores the selected version.

Prompt and skill delta

No new perpetual “self-improver”. A bounded reviewer/proposer can read the selected non-private evidence. All changes remain proposals until validated and approved.

A tool’s declaration, backend authorization and effective runtime visibility must agree. Adding a prompt mention is not implementing a capability. New role/configuration changes are hashed/versioned and exercised through the current native registry.

assistants/01_PRODUCT_AND_SCOPE.md

Owner-connected project assistants — product and rollout

Selected direction

Offer one Sophia Project Assistant template with task-specific methods. An owner can instead add the same cooperation skill to an existing knowledgeable assistant. Neither creates a new resource entitlement, imports conversation history automatically, or establishes per-Bot isolation.

The first useful episode is scattered-knowledge collection: selected laptop/desktop files, permitted applications and accessible prior research become a readable personal knowledge package. The owner inspects and refines the package in personal Sophia, then publishes a specific version through Share with the team. A job may be useful without ever being shared.

Sophia and the Bot communicate through tools and durable two-way messages from the first accepted integration. Questions, answers, guidance, blockers and useful partial results are part of gathering work, not a later enhancement. Ordinary software carries the messages; no lead model needs to paraphrase every exchange.

Personal first means the whole workflow

Job title, request, source inventory, messages, attachments, package, embeddings, notifications and intermediate interpretations are private to the authenticated owner. Do not place a private job in a team Paperclip company, project feed, public issue, shared runtime prompt or team search index. An eventual destination project does not change the initial audience.

The import is not automatically a kept personal memory. It is a versioned work product with explicit retention and sharing. Existing note Keep/Let go and Carry/Take back behavior remains distinct. A package is not squeezed into a note-size field or silently converted into a permanent personal identity fact.

Scope by gate

Gate User result Minimum machinery
PA-00 A harmless owner-authorized tool/message round-trip, plus provider limits recorded Actual OAuth flow and owner mapping; tested template/skill and optional webhook enrollment
PA-01 A personal collection job can ask, answer, be amended, upload a package, and survive observer restart Owner-private jobs/messages/storage; ingress validation; private UI; no team publication
PA-02 The owner reviews exact content, removes something and shares a chosen version to one team Immutable share preview, authenticated publication, source/read audience tests and withdrawal
PA-03 An exact web candidate or suitable external workflow is reviewed in the Bot environment Environment-specific capability proof, bounded task, real evidence and truthful blockers
PA-04 Two separately enrolled owners' assistants exchange useful project questions Explicit recipient edges, project export grants, peer bounds, no private-memory crossing or native cross-account assumption

PA-00/01/02 form the optional first assistant release. They do not block the core team release. The full live personal Companion is not required: humans can converse with the Bot through the private job thread. When personal Sophia synthesis is added, its separate runtime and allowance must be qualified.

Why use this resource

Choose it when the owner's existing knowledge, permitted source access, practiced application workflow, cloud computer, or explicitly contributed allowance adds value. Do not route ordinary public-web research to two external Bots merely to demonstrate parallelism; the native research route can handle that class of task. Server-hosted Sophia workers can also continue after a user disconnects.

Cloud independence is conditional. A cloud browser can work while the laptop is closed; a job that still depends on local commands or desktop-proxied network access must wait when that device is unreachable. Multi-hour reliability is a test requirement, not inferred from the word persistent. [GB-WORK; GB-COMPUTER]

Onboarding promise

Target no prompt writing or workflow design required, not unproven zero-setup provisioning. A native template import, provider login, connector authorization and routine setup may still be necessary. No account signup, purchase, permanent account link or template publication is performed by this pack. Use existing eligible subscribers for the first proof. [GB-TEMPLATE; GB-BILLING]

One assistant is offered by default; research/report/review are methods chosen for the job. Do not require a catalog of specialist Bots. A user can keep their established assistant's context without exporting all of it into Sophia.

Privacy and publication · tools/messages · computer use · setup · peer extension.

assistants/02_PRIVACY_AND_PUBLICATION.md

Personal ingestion, exact sharing and revocation

Domain objects and ownership

These are proposed application records. Bind them into the actual generated contracts and persistence layer; do not create a parallel production database from these examples.

Record Owner/audience Important properties
AssistantConnection Personal owner only Provider account subject, scopes, status, capabilities, credential references, revocation epoch; Bot label is display metadata
PersonalCollectionJob Personal owner only Purpose, selected collection scope, expected output, expiry, allowance policy, controller kind and generation
AssistantMessage Same job audience Trusted sender, reply/causal ID, kind, bounded content, permitted attachment references, sequence and delivery facts
KnowledgePackageVersion Personal owner only Immutable manifest, selected byte references/hashes, source coverage, findings, uncertainties, validation and retention
SharePreview Owner only Exact sanitized snapshot, destination, displayed version/hash, attachment list and expected membership/policy revision
SharedContribution One project Its own immutable published snapshot, attribution, permitted provenance, active/withdrawn state; never a read-through into private storage
PublicationReceipt Owner plus project-safe projection Exact approved digest, human actor, destination, policy/source revisions, operation key and result

Jobs/packages are asynchronous work. Do not insert fake personal conversation turns that the unimplemented Companion cannot answer. Reuse PR35 owner-only persistence and PR32 storage/parser primitives only after explicit integration; personal object paths, caches and authorization remain distinct from project reports.

Authorization boundary

Derive owner identity from verified session/OAuth credentials. Job IDs, actor fields, provider run IDs, email addresses and Bot display names are not authorization. Check owner, connection, job, grant revision, status and expiry on every request. For externally supplied IDs return the same non-enumerating denial shape whether the object is missing or belongs to someone else.

The Bot credential may retrieve its assigned job, exchange its permitted messages and submit a private candidate. It cannot publish to a team, choose another owner, add a team member, grant itself sources, or approve a share. Those operations require an authenticated human account and the application's current project policy. A natural-language message, a tool argument named approved, or a native provider approval is not Sophia publication consent.

Project membership does not authorize exporting all project data to the owner's assistant. A collection job receives either the owner's own purpose description or a separately approved, minimal project-context snapshot. Mark that outbound disclosure with recipient, content hash, permitted use and grant. A member's access to employer/client documents is not blanket permission to copy them to a personal provider.

Storage and all derived surfaces

Use owner-constrained reads and writes at the database boundary. Object-store keys and signed URLs are issued only through authorized readers; never rely on unpredictable URLs alone. Keep personal data out of team SSE/snapshots, shared search, vector indexes, cache keys and result notices. Request/error logging defaults to IDs/codes, not raw message bodies, filenames or provider errors that can echo content.

No team model receives private material to summarize it. Personal review assistance, if enabled, is a separate owner-scoped invocation with no team conversation memory. Do not send private job text to a shared Paperclip company even when only staff would see it. Initially controller_kind=sophia_personal_job owns private lifecycle; the team Paperclip scheduler has no entry. One controller per job remains the invariant. PA-04 uses Paperclip only for explicitly shared project work, not for private collection.

The privacy curtain is a device presentation control, not provider revocation. Hide and clear rendered personal content when it closes; do not cancel approved background collection merely because a view unmounts. No private push body or ARIA announcement is exposed in a team call. Unlocking reauthenticates the same person; it does not change the global session to another identity.

Package ingest and validation

The assistant prepares a report plus a source manifest, not a full-account archive. Coverage records requested, searched, actually read, omitted, inaccessible, duplicate and unsupported material with reasons. Distinguish original source, user note, earlier model report, recall and new inference. A recollection is not elevated into verified evidence by summarization.

Proposed pilot caps: 32 sources per package; 16 attached files; 25 MiB per file and 100 MiB total; 16 KiB per message; 512 KiB normalized text report; 8 KiB wake-free assignment summary. These are Sophia design limits, not provider entitlements. Large material is paged/staged explicitly, never silently truncated or automatically made public.

Upload to a single-purpose temporary object lease bound to owner/job/generation, maximum size and expected digest. Verify actual size, media type and SHA-256 before admission. Reject path traversal, active HTML, executable archives, decompression bombs and unsafe remote fetch URLs. Stage unknown files for safe inspection; never execute an imported script or let a package name mutate storage paths. Reuse the data-only report parser. Disable unapproved remote images and tracking loads. A cloud path or provider chat URL is not proof that bytes were received.

Keep package versions immutable. Edits produce a new version. An assistant-reported hash is checked against stored bytes; it is not trusted merely because it has the right shape. Retain useful partial results with explicit missing coverage.

Exact share transaction

  1. The owner selects the version, content/attachments and destination. Build a separate team-safe snapshot; remove unselected source bodies, private paths, account identifiers and hidden metadata. Selected summaries with non-shared evidence disclose that verification is limited.
  2. Show exactly that snapshot and its attachments in the sharing preview. Compute a digest on canonical selected bytes plus disclosure metadata. No stale or invisible selection may be included.
  3. On Share, recheck same human, current project membership/export/import policy, source eligibility, expected package version, preview digest and operation key. Do not re-run a model between preview and commit.
  4. Record approval, target contribution and publication outbox atomically. Keep target invisible until all authorized bytes exist and verify. For a separate object store, use an idempotent staged-copy worker and transactional final publication; never announce success before the source reader can serve the complete version.
  5. A lost response reconciles under the same operation key; same key/different payload is conflict. Return one receipt. Sharing does not accept a mission proposal or spawn research automatically.

A changed package or share selection invalidates the previous preview. Membership removal between preview and commit refuses publication. The project receives a snapshot with its own controlled lifecycle, not a foreign key that allows arbitrary private-version reads. Physical byte dedupe, if later introduced, must retain separate authorization references and non-leaking deletion semantics.

Updates, withdrawal and erasure

Private edits never auto-update project content. Explicit updates generate a new share preview and version. An owner may withdraw a shared contribution under the existing project rule; future source/context reads are fenced immediately. Relevant Sophia-owned workers and derived summaries are invalidated/rebuilt using the actual source dependency contract. For externally hosted Bots, fence future reads/publication and show that provider-retained copies may remain.

Deleting a private package or erasing personal data does not silently remove an already shared project version. Offer the separate withdrawal action and enumerate active shares without exposing another owner's records. Revoking a connection blocks new tool access and wakes, retains only necessary control/erasure tombstones and does not claim native computer shutdown. Native provider conversation deletion is a separate owner action.

Proposed retention: incomplete upload objects expire within 24 hours; terminal personal job message/source-inventory content defaults to 30 days unless the owner keeps it; received packages remain until owner deletion; identifier-only dedupe/erasure records follow a separately reviewed minimum retention. Deadlines are implementation policy proposals, not running schedules. PA-01 must implement deterministic cleanup and fake-clock tests before accepting private data; a real timer has its own deployment authorization.

Required leakage tests

Test two owners plus a project administrator, direct API/object reads, list counts, search/embeddings, SSE, cache keys, notifications, error responses, tracing, exports, a team model retrieval, and a call/lock transition. Test a secret-looking source title and excluded attachment. Private staging cannot pass merely because its main screen is hidden.

Two-way tools, messaging and truthful execution

Product contract and provider boundary

Sophia tools expose deterministic records and mutation receipts. Messages carry questions, findings, replies and guidance. Both travel through one authenticated remote MCP surface, not a second agent loop or model relay. The operations here are proposed Sophia contracts; no provider URL or undocumented RPC is invented.

Grok routine webhooks are documented to accept an authenticated POST and JSON payload. A 200 establishes activation, not result delivery. The native Bot conversation remains a recovery/approval surface. External run enumeration, in-turn steering, precise cancellation, quota inspection and API idempotency are not assumed. [GB-ROUTINES]

Minimal operation set for PA-01

Operation Trusted scope Result
sophia_read_job Connected owner; exact admitted job and generation Bounded current purpose, constraints, source/export permissions, receipt and pending-message cursor
sophia_read_messages Same job/owner/generation Ordered eligible messages, explicit has_more and next cursor; delivery is not incorporation
sophia_send_message Server-derived sender; same job Stored question/answer/finding/blocker/checkpoint with stable idempotency key
sophia_claim_job Current ready or continuation-ready job Atomic claim and scope receipt; no duplicate active claim
sophia_prepare_upload Job and owner; declared safe media/size/hash Short-lived upload lease, never a general storage credential
sophia_submit_package Active claim; current generation Private candidate receipt after server validation, or actionable refusal
sophia_finish_turn Current claim only Provider-self-reported yielded/finished/blocked checkpoint; not independently verified provider stop

No publish/share/delete-team/approve-native operation is included. Owner actions in Sophia use its ordinary authenticated API and separate permission checks. Do not expose an all-purpose shell or HTTP proxy through MCP.

A model-reported native session ID or Bot label is retained as reported, not provider-attested. The trusted actor is the enrolled connection subject. Local display uses owner + provider + reported label without claiming per-Bot cryptographic isolation.

Message classes and authority

question, answer, guidance, finding, blocker, checkpoint, handoff and ack are the initial classes. Content has reply_to, causal_root, assignment revision and permitted evidence references. The backend derives sender and audience; no arbitrary from or target owner can be supplied.

Messages are task data, not authorization. A suggested new source or broader action becomes an owner decision and a revised grant before use. A valid owner reply within existing scope may guide work without repeated consent dialogs. Approval to run a provider command is not approval to publish in Sophia.

One question should collect related ambiguities rather than start a separate thread per minor detail. A finding can be retained quietly; only a genuine blocker or useful result needs attention. ack never triggers another wake.

State dimensions (do not flatten them)

Job: draft → ready → active → waiting_for_owner / waiting_for_device / waiting_for_peer → candidate_ready → closed. Withdrawal is terminal for new work; failure can preserve a useful candidate. New work after a withdrawal requires a new owner-authorized assignment, not a late reply.

Dispatch: not_sent → intent_recorded → accepted / rejected / unknown. A request timeout is unknown, not rejected. Never retry an unknown provider activation blindly.

Claim: unclaimed → claimed → yielded / finished / abandoned_unknown. Claim expiry alone cannot prove the provider stopped. A new conflicting claim is refused until reconciliation or an explicitly reviewed fresh assignment with preserved uncertainty.

Delivery: stored → fetched → incorporation_reported → outcome_checked. Fetch is server-observable. Incorporation is agent-reported unless a relevant outcome/check confirms it. Do not display applied from a POST alone.

Publication: private → share_preview → human_approved_pending_copy → shared / refused. None of the preceding run states grants publication.

No job/process state is inferred from observer disconnection or a model's fluent final sentence. Source reception and product acceptance have their own evidence.

Activation, resume and uncertainty

Record dispatch intent before effects with job/generation/notification identity. A webhook carries only an opaque job reference and event kind. Keep webhook URL/key backend-only. Validate enrolled HTTPS origin and path, block private/link-local/metadata destinations and unapproved redirects, pin the credential to its exact destination, limit response logging and redact the secret. Re-registration requires the authenticated owner; connection IDs do not let a caller post to arbitrary URLs.

The provider has not been shown to support idempotent activation. Serialize one outstanding activation per connection for the pilot. After a timeout, wait for a claim or ask the owner to inspect native state; do not run a retry loop. An application-side duplicate claim prevents duplicate source delivery/publication, not duplicate provider consumption.

For a busy job, queue guidance and let the Bot read it at a meaningful boundary. Do not fire another routine just to simulate in-turn steer. For a yielded job, persist the checkpoint, then activate once when a substantive reply arrives, if that continuation path was actually qualified. Coalesce multiple pending changes. If continuation cannot be proven, present an owner-started native resume path and keep the live orchestration gate open.

An owner may initiate collection directly in the Bot. It still retrieves an admitted private job and exchanges messages. This may qualify tool/message behavior before webhook setup, but the product must not label Sophia-initiated activation ready until the webhook path passes.

Budgets and loop control

Proposed pilot defaults: one active collection per connection, one outstanding activation, no periodic model polling, maximum six substantive exchanges before a checkpoint, one coalesced notification per unread epoch and bounded response sizes. These are software limits on Sophia's route, not a provider compute cap. Limit changes require a new owner-approved policy when they expand the contribution.

Use fake time and synthetic replies to test waiting/expiry. Never burn a real allowance to manufacture a limit. Do not create standing routines from this pack; the owner enrolls an event-only routine with no schedule for the first pilot.

Withdrawal and safety

Software revocation immediately prevents new Sophia wakes, claims, reads and writes under the old epoch. Reject late results into team sources; preserve an allowed private partial candidate only under explicit current owner policy. Tell the owner how to stop the Bot natively. Report provider activity as unverified until actual evidence arrives. Do not expose a button labelled Stop Bot when all it does is withdraw the application job.

For consequential external effects, the first route is unsuitable without a verified mediation/control boundary. Read-only tasks can still perform temporary file processing in their authorized workspace; read-only means no change to original source or external account state, not that no local computation occurs.

Test path

Prove owner → Bot request, Bot → owner question, owner reply, Bot retrieval, changed package result and durable receipt. Repeat after Sophia restart, connector refresh, lost submission response, source withdrawal and a native login/device wait. In PA-04 add cross-owner recipient edges only after the private flow is accepted.

assistants/04_COMPUTER_USE_AND_RESOURCES.md

Computer-use and contributed-resource qualification

Supported environment categories

Category Evidence boundary Initial use
Hosted Bot browser/computer Provider documentation describes persistent browser, files and terminal; reliability unmeasured here Selected account collection and read-only review of an exact internet-accessible preview
Native local commands/files Separately approved local-execution path; device must be reachable Inventory and collection from explicitly selected folders; originals unchanged
Desktop-proxied network Depends on actual desktop/network route; do not assume all terminal traffic follows it Internal preview only after exact route and disconnect behavior are tested
Local visual GUI via Cua Driver Third-party installation/OS permissions, separate local-command policy Optional later compatibility task, not first-release dependency

Documentation sources: GB-WORK, GB-COMPUTER, GB-CUA. Their claims are capability inputs, not a benchmark or acceptance result. Native provider approvals, login, MFA and CAPTCHA remain owner actions. Do not automate credential capture, bypass a site's controls, strip frame/security headers, or infer a general right to scrape private assistant histories.

Work selection

Prefer structured permitted connectors and file exports when available; visual interaction is for gaps where it adds value. A source inaccessible through a supported route is listed as inaccessible. Account-wide history crawls and broad device scans are not the default. For local input, disclose copying selected material to a cloud provider as a separate data movement; it is not implied by a later team-share permission.

After collection, a cloud analysis phase can continue on explicitly approved copied input while the laptop is offline. Work still needing an unsynced local file must show waiting_for_device. Closing Sophia alone should not stop admitted server-side work, either native or Bot. Multi-hour tasks need useful checkpoints and recovery evidence; duration alone does not justify a new provider.

Browser-review assignment

Bind preview/deployment URL, exact source candidate/commit, allowed network targets, test-account role, viewport/journeys and forbidden effects. Use a staging/preview account with no production authority. Return steps, expected/actual behavior, repeatability, timestamp, screenshots/logs and limits. Screenshots may contain personal/client data and follow the same private-first rule unless a specifically project-scoped review was authorized.

Native visual review does not replace executable assertions. Compare against Playwright or the relevant existing application checks. A provider screenshot alone is not source identity; the preview service should expose a non-secret candidate marker where possible, and the Bot must report if it cannot verify it. Do not synthesize evidence for inaccessible journeys.

Test fresh and resumed sessions, changed screen state, stale authentication, device disconnection, a removed source and a late result. Separate necessary human steps (login/approval) from avoidable assistance. Record quality, intervention burden, completion, useful partial output and observed usage; no invented success percentage.

Resource accounting

The connection contributes one owner account's available Bot allowance. Several Bots or routines on it are not separate balances. Current billing documentation describes eligible paid Cursor/linked individual Grok access and non-stacking grants; with on-demand disabled included allowance exhaustion stops work, while enabled overage limits are not hard mid-run cutoffs. [GB-BILLING]

For the pilot require the owner to confirm included-usage mode and identify any connected billable tools. Record whether the setting was owner-attested, observed in UI or provider-attested, with date. Do not claim Sophia continuously enforces a provider setting or knows remaining capacity without a verified API. Team-plan defaults can differ; verify rather than assume. No auto-purchase, link movement, added API key, paid fallback, another owner's account or unapproved external service charge.

Provider-managed model selection is not dsh-like control. Missing reasoning/model controls remain unsupported; choose task/output boundaries rather than inventing settings. Sophia hosting, storage, message processing and any personal Companion inference remain separate costs.

Connection readiness

connected proves authentication only. qualified_private_import, qualified_web_review, qualified_local_collection, qualified_wake_resume and qualified_project_peers are independent evidence flags bound to actual provider/client/version/configuration. Configuration changes or material provider regressions invalidate the relevant flags. No green universal-ready label from a successful MCP tools/list.

assistants/05_SETUP_AND_QUALIFICATION.md

Guided setup and qualification

One template or one skill on an existing assistant

Provide the literal Project Assistant template and knowledge-import skill. The template is a reviewed starting configuration, not a live clone of our account. Use a clean template authoring account/environment with no customer content, credentials, private memories or internal endpoints before any separately approved publication.

Template import and Bot duplication are different provider operations; neither is proof that a newly created copy has the user's existing conversations. A knowledgeable existing assistant can use the cooperation/import skill instead. Some documentation describes relevant template memories while duplication excludes learned memory: inspect the actual exported package rather than rely on either phrase as an automatic privacy guarantee. Custom MCP connection material requires separate setup. [GB-TEMPLATE; GB-WORK]

Enrollment sequence

  1. In personal Sophia, explain provider data handling, account scope, native permissions, billing limitations and what is not shared. The owner selects an existing eligible account; Sophia neither buys nor resells a subscription.
  2. Complete the actual provider import/skill step. Review the details before installation. Link eligible accounts only in the provider's native flow, with explicit warning about any permanent/non-stacking relationship.
  3. Authorize the Sophia remote MCP through a supported OAuth flow. Use a reviewed OAuth server/provider: authorization code with PKCE, state/nonce protection, exact registered redirect matching, audience/resource-bound tokens, short-lived access and rotated/revocable refresh credentials where supported. Use observed client metadata rather than hardcoded guessed callbacks. No wildcard redirects or secrets placed in messages as a workaround.
  4. Sophia resolves the verified token subject to the signed-in owner and a specific enrolled connection. Scopes are narrowly personal-job/read-message/write-message/upload. No team publication tool is issued.
  5. For Sophia activation, the owner configures one event-only routine using the routine instruction, then enters its URL/key in an owner-only secure Sophia enrollment form. Store the secret server-side, redact it from logs and never return it to the model. If a secure supported input path is unavailable, do not expose it through chat.
  6. Run one harmless round-trip: retrieve synthetic job, ask a question, owner replies in Sophia, retrieve reply, return corrected text, then revoke the test connection and confirm denial. A separate safe webhook test qualifies start and continuation.
  7. Show exactly which capabilities passed and which remain unavailable. A failed connection does not produce a ready label or silently change provider.

Known provider boundary

First-party support documented a custom-MCP OAuth registration incompatibility with Cloudflare Access and corrected an unsafe suggestion to configure arbitrary secret headers. Treat that as a compatibility warning, not proof every OAuth server fails. Qualify Sophia's actual auth server on the intended desktop/client and refuse a credential-in-chat fallback. [GB-OAUTH]

No public provisioning API was verified for buying subscriptions, importing/configuring a user's Bot or enumerating its private memory. Design guided setup, not a fictitious fully in-app Create Bot button.

Pilot configuration choices

Use one owner, one connection, one active assignment and a non-sensitive collection example first. On-demand disabled by the owner; no purchases, account mutations or production tools. Keep a native open-Bot recovery path, but no browser automation impersonating the owner or scraping provider conversations to obtain results.

Check OAuth connect, expired access refresh, restart, owner mismatch, revocation, tool-schema mismatch, partial upload, uncertain wake, and masked errors. Scope any real provider usage with a separate human grant. A test run performs real work and can consume usage; it is not free merely because its label is Test.

Exit

PA-00 ends with a capability/binding report and one working authenticated exchange, or a precise unsupported boundary. Do not spend an unbounded mission building around undocumented endpoints. Local fixtures can continue without a provider account, but they do not close live acceptance.

assistants/06_PEER_COOPERATION.md

Later cross-owner peer cooperation

Preserve the one-template idea

Two owners can connect copies of the same Project Assistant and receive different roles per admitted assignment: competitor evidence, customer evidence, design alternative or independent review. The current mandate is task data; it does not mutate the permanent template or increase resource permissions.

Native Bot messaging/group features are evidence of provider-local cooperation, not proof of arbitrary personal cross-account control. Sophia's scoped software relay provides the cross-owner path. Tools transport messages and evidence; Sophia's reasoning concentrates on scope, significant disagreements and synthesis. [GB-WORK]

Enroll the team edge explicitly

Only PA-04 introduces project peer recipient edges. Both owners must contribute their connections, allowed tasks, data scopes and spending policy. Project policy must permit disclosure to those external account environments. An owner cannot bind another person's assistant or cause their account to spend merely by mentioning its name.

Use an operational work assignment in Paperclip if that project has selected Paperclip. Store a single work mapping and route adapter; do not let the private inbox controller and Paperclip both continue the same assignment. A personal collection stays personal even when its owner participates in a shared project. Shared messages may refer only to project-published source versions or separately approved outbound snapshots.

Interaction pattern

First collect independent findings when diverse evidence is useful. Then permit a small number of purposeful questions/challenges. Finally return revised contributions with sources, what changed, uncertainty and the exact candidate. Sophia compares contributions with the mission and presents a proposal; it does not automatically accept consensus or count two similar model answers as independent empirical confirmation.

Peer envelopes retain actual connection sender, source/assignment revision, recipient binding, reply and causal chain, bounded content and permitted evidence references. Validate every reference for the receiving owner/project before delivery. A peer cannot elevate a job from review to deploy, alter another owner's reserve, access their personal memory or issue direct admin requests.

Wake and recovery

Use durable inboxes and substantive reply wakes, never synchronous model polling. Coalesce notifications; receipt acknowledgements do not wake the sender. Detect reciprocal waits and return a best-effort partial answer or a bounded lead decision instead of indefinite deadlock. Limit chain depth and exchanges in the accepted policy. Reconcile unknown remote activity before retry/reassign; a transport receipt does not prove incorporated guidance.

PA-04 acceptance includes two real owners, their correct payer attribution, one question whose answer changes the work, restart with pending mail, a removed member and a late reply. A market-research demonstration is appropriate here, not as a substitute for PA-01/02's privacy proof or the native three-engineer release.

assistants/07_MCP_API_AND_STORAGE_BINDINGS.md

Proposed MCP, application API and storage binding

Status: proposed design target in this pack; not deployed OpenAPI, SQL or provider tooling. The implementation goal authors the next available contract amendment and migration only after refreshing A10/A11 reservations. Existing API prefix is read from the checkout; paths below are proposed relative resources, not a client-ready URL list.

Application service map

Proposed resource/operation Caller Transaction responsibility
personal/assistant-connections create/read/revoke Authenticated human owner Enroll verified subject/secret ref/capabilities; atomic grant epoch update and wake fence
personal/collection-jobs create/read/amend/withdraw Authenticated owner Immutable mandate revisions, source selection, allowance mode, one continuation owner
personal/collection-jobs/{job}/messages read/send Owner or scoped connector Owner/job authorization, ordered sequence, idempotency and reply validation
personal/knowledge-packages version/read/delete Owner or submit-only connector Validate byte manifest, immutable version, owner-only source readers, cleanup tombstones
personal/share-previews create/read Human owner only Materialize exact sanitized snapshot and selected metadata before consent
personal/share-previews/{preview}/publish Human owner only Recheck owner, target membership/policy, version/hash; receipt/outbox; no model in commit
projects/{project}/contributions read/withdraw Project members / authorized source owner Serve only published snapshot; current membership, withdrawal and derived eligibility

MCP calls invoke those same application use cases after translating verified token subject to connection/job scope. Do not call HTTP handlers as authorization substitutes or expose the internal SQL service role to a provider. Reuse current OpenAPI generation and response validators. A missing deployed handler remains unavailable; the frontend cannot invent success from a schema example.

Proposed persistent fields and indexes

Use owner_id as the personal partition key with RLS/role checks on all content-bearing tables. Keep job_id, connection_id, generation, mandate_revision, request_key, payload_digest and current grant eligibility. Unique keys include (owner_id, request_key) for human commands, (connection_id, job_id, request_key) for connector writes, (job_id, sequence) for messages and (owner_id, package_id, version) for packages.

Message receipts do not keep plaintext after owner erasure. Hashes of private words can also reveal information; erasure retains only opaque operation IDs/erasure fences necessary to reject stale retries, not content digests or source titles. Replay under an erased key returns the existing erased/revoked disposition and writes nothing.

Share metadata stores project-safe attribution separately from personal provenance. The project-facing record must not expose the private package's contents, list endpoint, hidden-source IDs or raw local path. An owner-only share mapping supports correction/take-back. Team views use the copied public manifest, not unrestricted joins into personal tables.

Uploaded bytes

Use the existing Storage-only byte-store interface after M03 integration, with separate owner-bound logical namespaces and exact digest verification. Database authorization mediates lease creation and reads. Upload grants are single-purpose, time/size-limited and only write one target object. They are not provider credential custody. No native cloud path is accepted as a completed upload.

Enforce content validation before parse/index, safe data-only preview, attached-file coverage and explicit failure. Signed upload URLs may be used as scoped transport capabilities only when that flow is supported and not logged to shared transcripts; otherwise use direct capped tool content for the pilot. Do not ask for arbitrary custom secret headers in Grok's model-visible arguments.

Fences and race order

For every effect: current connection/job eligibility → lock current owner/job record → dedupe under same key → compare expected revision/generation → perform or stage effect → record receipt/outbox → deliver. Withdrawal increments/fences the job before attempting optional remote notification. A provider callback received later cannot restore eligibility.

For publication with a separate object store, perform prepare/copy/verify/finalize with idempotent stages. Only the finalize transaction exposes the team snapshot and emits the project-safe event. Retry after lost response returns the same contribution. A failed copy emits no shared partial package. The original private package remains independent.

Privacy-aware observability

Record codes, IDs, byte counts, capability/evidence class and elapsed time. Personal logs and job events have owner-level access; no private content in global analytics, LangSmith traces, public GitHub issues or Paperclip company comments. A provider error must be normalized before logging because it may echo the prompt or account name. Test errors and secondary indexes, not just happy-path RLS.

Proposed schema files

Connection · Job · Message · Package · Share.

These schemas constrain shapes. Server-side identity, membership, scope and transaction rules above remain mandatory even when a payload passes JSON Schema.

coordination/01_CONTROL_SUPPORT_MATRIX.md

Control-support matrix — first engineering deliverable

Design rule: a configuration field, an upstream function and a live qualified capability are three different things. This table is the starting audit, not a declaration that every row is implemented. SCM-00/01/02 replace “qualify” with exact source symbols, effective settings, test IDs and actual receipts.

Status vocabulary

existing_source means inspected Sophia code; candidate_source means an unmerged reviewed candidate; upstream_contract means a donor declaration; planned means new Sophia work; unqualified means no live proof for this composition. Unsupported and unknown remain distinct. All controls must be scoped to project/work/attempt/resource and an immutable configuration revision.

Matrix

Control Scope and change boundary dsh path Owner-native path Enforcement and evidence
Provider/model Recorded attempt identity; new episode or explicitly qualified transition Merged M02 journals/resumes recorded identity (existing_source); PR32 adds per-attempt research routes in candidate_source. Live role qualification remains specific to the route. Set native session override before launch, verify actual route. S08 binding. Requested, resolved and observed IDs; mismatch holds, no alias-based success.
Reasoning effort Provider-supported value at the same boundary as model config M02 route includes effort; not a portable universal level. Per-native route/version; unknown support cannot be silently ignored. Request/protocol evidence plus effective configuration; never treat “high” as a measured quality result.
